author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two teenagers have been charged in connection with the fire that badly damaged Kimball Castle in Gilford last year, the New Hampshire State Fire Marshal announced Friday. Joshua Pittman, 18, of Dover, faces a felony conspiracy-to-commit-arson charge and misdemeanor criminal trespass. Peyton Eastman, 19, of Portsmouth, faces felony arson and misdemeanor criminal trespass.

The August 27, 2025, fire was treated as suspicious after flames swept through the historic stone property. Investigators said the building was damaged so severely that demolition was expected. The castle, built in the late 1890s and listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1982, is a familiar landmark overlooking Lake Winnipesaukee.

Authorities arrested Pittman on September 1 and Eastman on September 2 before announcing the charges Friday. Both were released on personal recognizance and are scheduled for arraignment October 8 in Laconia District Court. The filings are accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Officials did not announce a motive or disclose additional details about how investigators connected the two teenagers to the fire.
dek: State fire investigators announced felony charges against two teenagers more than a year after flames badly damaged the historic Lake Winnipesaukee landmark.
headline: Two teenagers charged in fire that damaged historic Kimball Castle
